text:
alex: noticing a spike in apiserver request latencies and controller-manager queue backlog in eu-west1 around 08:12 UTC, correlated with multiple etcd leader changes
mar ia: you mean leader elections or leader stepdowns?
jordan: logs show raft leader stepdown + increased proposal latency, also a bunch of SYN_RECV on the NAT gateway around that time
alex: correct — multiple leader elections (3x) in ~90s, apiserver 5xxs and controller-manager backlog increased, GPU pod startups timing out
ops-bot: Incident detected: apiserver-503-spike-eu-west1. Pager duty notified to oncall-sre
sam: can someone paste the etcd leader-change snippet?
alex: here are the tail lines from etcd:
```
2026-03-20T08:12:03Z etcd1 raft: leader changed from 10.0.1.7 to 10.0.2.5
2026-03-20T08:12:34Z etcd2 raft: leader changed from 10.0.2.5 to 10.0.3.9
2026-03-20T08:13:12Z etcd3 raft: leader changed from 10.0.3.9 to 10.0.1.7
```
jordan: we also saw >1k conntrack entries in TIME_WAIT on the NATs and SNAT port exhaustion was near threshold, so kube-proxy endpoints churn + apiserver requests were getting delayed
lee: that explains controller-manager retries — it keeps hitting apiserver and queues pile up
maria: what triggered NAT pressure? any bulk jobs or gpu onboarding?
alex: burst of GPU node attach events from dedicated pools (autoscaler ramp) + image pulls causing egress bursts; these requests go through region NAT and cause ephemeral port exhaustion
sam: mitigation options: 1) throttle node attach rate on provisioner 2) increase SNAT capacity / use more NAT IPs 3) temporarily route control-plane egress through peered path
jordan: short-term action: reduce kube-controller-manager concurrent reconciles to 5 and lower apiserver `--max-requests-inflight` to reduce load. Will push canary config?
lee: +1 on lowering concurrency. I'll open a rollout PR for controller-manager replicas/flags, canary to staging first
maria: also we should add a guard to provisioner to limit attach concurrency per region to avoid thundering on NATs
alex: doing `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-controller-manager -o yaml` to patch config now
ops-bot: Deploy triggered: patch/kcm-concurrency-reduce (canary) by lee
sam: reminder: this is also a cost/latency tradeoff — if we throttle attach, customer onboarding latency rises, but prevents control plane meltdown
jordan: medium-term: consider moving image pulls to private registry endpoints with VPC egress or add more NAT gateways per AZ; also add healthcheck to detect port exhaustion early
maria: proposal: add control-plane egress fallback policy in routing (if NAT port usage >80% route supervisor calls via peered path). File an RFC?
alex: agree. Also tweak etcd election timeouts? leader elections were frequent because IOPS + scheduling pauses on etcd nodes during compaction. We can increase heartbeat and election timeouts slightly to tolerate short I/O stalls
lee: careful — increasing election timeout masks real failures. Let's combine with root cause (IO/peering) fixes and smaller bump as temporary measure
sam: action items: 
- lee: rollout controller-manager concurrency patch (canary) — due 20m
- alex: add rate limit to provisioner for region attach — due EOD
- jordan: open NAT capacity ticket + short-term IP pool expansion — due 1h
- maria: draft RFC for egress-fallback + monitoring for SNAT ports — due 2d
ops-bot: Incident updated: mitigations in flight, monitoring spike suppressed
alex: monitoring now shows apiserver latency dropping and controller-manager queue shrinking, will keep watching for next 30m :thumbsup:
